> **What this case shows** — push-off (the propulsive second hump of the vertical GRF, driven chiefly by the
> ankle plantarflexors) weakens with age. The [Kruskal-Wallis
> sibling](../gait-grf-pushoff-kruskal-gaitrec/index.qmd) showed push-off separates gait pathologies; here
> we ask, within *healthy* adults, how fast it declines with age. Each subject's push-off peak comes from
> the **certified** `grfLandmarks`; the **newly-authored** `linearRegression` regresses it on age,
> reproducing **`scipy.stats.linregress`** **bit-for-bit** and base R **`lm`** to machine precision. The
> slope is **−0.012 BW per decade** (t(206)=−4.6, **p~7e-6**, R²=0.094) — a modest but highly significant
> healthy-aging propulsion decline.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `grfLandmarks()` per subject → push-off peak → `linearRegression(age, push_off)`.
**Way of thinking** — a correlation says *whether* two things move together; a regression slope says *how
fast*. Reporting the slope in interpretable units (BW per decade) turns an association into an actionable
rate — and the R² keeps you honest about how much it explains.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioMoCap::grfLandmarks()`, `PhysioAnalysis::linearRegression()`.
:::

## Proposition

In GaitRec healthy controls (n=208, ages 15-78), the vertical-GRF push-off peak declines with age at slope
−0.00120 BW/year (−0.012 BW/decade; intercept 1.144 BW), t(206)=−4.61, p~7.0e-6, R²=0.094;
`linearRegression` reproduces `scipy.stats.linregress` bit-for-bit and base R `lm` to machine precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is a rate and the op that measures it: within healthy adults, how fast does push-off
propulsion decline with age, and does a simple OLS regression reproduce the reference?** The sibling folds
compared groups; this one fits a line and reads off its slope.

## Challenge & approach

For each healthy control we take the push-off peak (the 3rd landmark of `grfLandmarks`, certified in the
[gait-grf-gaitrec](../gait-grf-gaitrec/index.qmd) case) from the body-weight- and time-normalised vertical
GRF, pair it with the subject's age, and fit `linearRegression` — checking the slope, R² and slope p-value
against `scipy.stats.linregress` and base R `lm`.

```
GaitRec healthy controls (n=208, ages 15-78): grfLandmarks push-off peak vs age
  OLS: push_off = 1.144 - 0.00120 * age   (BW)      →  -0.012 BW / decade
  t(206) = -4.61,  p ~ 7.0e-6,  R2 = 0.094
     vs scipy.stats.linregress → |diff| = 0 (bit-for-bit)
     vs base R lm              → |diff| ~ 1e-18 (machine precision)
```

## Data

**GaitRec (Horsak et al. 2020)**: vertical-GRF push-off peak and age for the healthy controls (n=208, ages
15-78), shod, standardised speed, baseline sessions (one per-subject mean curve). Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Push-off peak vs age for 208 healthy controls, with the OLS fit (red) and its 95% confidence band. The line slopes gently down — −0.012 BW per decade — and the scatter is wide (R²=0.094): age shifts the average push-off but explains under a tenth of the between-person variance. The fit equals scipy.stats.linregress and base R lm.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the downward slope is the healthy-aging propulsion decline, small per year but highly
significant across the cohort; the wide scatter (low R²) is the honest caveat — age is one modest
contributor among many to how hard a given person pushes off.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **slope** | **−0.00120 BW/year** (−0.012 /decade) |
| intercept | 1.144 BW |
| **R²** | **0.094** |
| t (df 206) | −4.61 |
| −log₁₀ p | 5.2 (p ~ 7.0e-6) |
| n (healthy controls) | 208 |
| vs `scipy.stats.linregress` (\|diff\|) | **0** (bit-for-bit) |
| vs base R `lm` (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~1e-18) |

The fit equals scipy exactly and base R to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/pushoff_age_regression_summary.csv`](artifacts/pushoff_age_regression_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`linearRegression` reproduces the reference on the certified `grfLandmarks`. The transferable takeaway:
**report the slope, not just the correlation — "push-off falls ~0.012 BW per decade" is a rate a clinician
can use, while the R² (0.094) keeps the claim honest about scatter. Reducing a force curve to a certified
landmark and fitting one line turns healthy aging into a measured propulsion trajectory.**

## Open questions

- The healthy-control age distribution is young-skewed (only 2 subjects over 70), so a single linear slope
  may understate the decline at older ages where ankle push-off power drops more steeply; denser older
  sampling or a spline fit would refine the trajectory. The analysis is cross-sectional, not longitudinal.
  The linear slope is the most interpretable first-order rate. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| GRF landmarks (peaks, trough) | `grfLandmarks()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Simple OLS regression | `linearRegression()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Correlation (r) | `correlationTest()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **slope** — the change in the outcome per unit predictor; report it in interpretable units (here BW per
  decade) with its p-value.
- **R²** — the fraction of variance explained; a significant slope with a small R² (as here) means a real
  but modest effect against wide individual variation — say so.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioMoCap); library(PhysioAnalysis)

push_off <- apply(hc_vGRF, 1, function(v) grfLandmarks(v)[3])   # 3rd landmark = push-off peak
linearRegression(age, push_off)   # slope, intercept, R2, t, p -- bit-for-bit vs scipy.stats.linregress and base R lm
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/pushoff_age_regression_summary.csv`](artifacts/pushoff_age_regression_summary.csv), and
[`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the slope, intercept, R², the slope t and p, the bit-exact match against
scipy and the machine-precision match against base R lm, the negative-slope direction, the sample size, and
the honestly noted scope (authors the new linearRegression op; push-off from the certified grfLandmarks;
young-skewed ages; cross-sectional association, not longitudinal change).
